title: Nabta Playa
summary: Nabta Playa is a basin in the Nubian Desert of southern Egypt, about 500 miles south of Cairo. UNESCO describes hunter-gatherer settlement there from about 11,000 years ago, early pottery, and megalithic structures built between 4,600 and 3,400 BC; excavators also mapped a small stone circle with sight lines, one of which roughly matches the summer solstice sunrise.

uncertainty.note: Years are astronomical. Start converts the UNESCO figure "about 11,000 BP" using BP = years before 1950 (1950 - 11000 = -9050); end is 3,400 BC = -3399. The 1998 Archaeology report instead dates the megalith-bearing deposits to 7,000-6,700 years ago, which conflicts with UNESCO's 4,600-3,400 BC; the record spans both. The id year -8000 is a round placeholder.

reviewer_note: Least sure: dating. UNESCO gives megaliths as 4,600-3,400 BC but Archaeology (1998) reports deposits 7,000-6,700 years ago; I span both and did not choose. Settlement start is UNESCO's "about 11,000 BP" converted with BP = 1950. Wikidata point is a basin centre, not a specific structure. The astronomical meaning is described by the source as speculation, so the summary says only that one sight line roughly matches the solstice sunrise.
